title: Chapter 73 — Stubb and Flask kill a Right Whale; and Then Have a Talk
paragraphs: over Him.

Keep in mind that all this while a Sperm Whale's enormous head has been hanging from the Pequod's side. But we must leave it hanging there a while longer, until we get a chance to deal with it. Other matters are pressing just now, and the best we can do for the head at present is to pray to heaven that the tackles hold.

Now, during the past night and morning, the Pequod had gradually drifted into a sea which, by its occasional patches of yellow brit, gave unusual signs that Right Whales were near — a species of the Leviathan that few supposed to be lurking anywhere nearby at this particular time. And though all hands commonly disdained the capture of those inferior creatures; and though the Pequod was not commissioned to cruise for them at all; and though she had passed numbers of them near the Crozets without lowering a boat — yet now that a Sperm Whale had been brought alongside and beheaded, to everyone's surprise the announcement was made that a Right Whale should be captured that day, if the opportunity arose.

We did not have long to wait. Tall spouts were sighted to leeward, and two boats, Stubb's and Flask's, were sent after them. They pulled farther and farther off until the men at the masthead could barely see them. Then suddenly, far away, they saw a great heap of churning white water, and soon word came down from aloft that one or both boats must be fast. After a while the boats came into plain view, being dragged straight toward the ship by the whale that had them in tow. The monster came so close to the hull that at first he seemed to mean it harm; but then, within three rods of the planking, he suddenly plunged down in a whirlpool and vanished completely, as if diving under the keel. "Cut, cut!" the ship shouted to the boats, which for an instant looked certain to be smashed against the vessel's side. But since they still had plenty of line in the tubs and the whale was not sounding very fast, they paid out rope freely while rowing with all their strength to get ahead of the ship. For a few minutes things were extremely critical: as they let out the taut line in one direction and worked their oars in another, the opposing pulls threatened to drag them under. Yet all they needed to gain was a few feet. They kept at it until they gained them — and at that instant a swift tremor ran like lightning along the keel, as the strained line, scraping along beneath the ship, suddenly surfaced under her bows, snapping and quivering and shaking off its drips so that they fell like bits of broken glass on the water; the whale also came up into sight beyond, and once again the boats were free to fly. But the worn-out whale slowed down and, blindly changing course, swung around the ship's stern with the two boats in tow, so that they made a full circle.

Meanwhile, they hauled more and more on their lines, till, closely flanking him on both sides, Stubb answered Flask lance for lance; and so round and round the Pequod the battle went, while the multitudes of sharks that had been swimming around the Sperm Whale's body rushed to the fresh blood that was spilled, thirstily drinking at every new gash, as the eager Israelites drank at the new fountains that burst from the smitten rock.
At last his spout thickened, and with a horrible roll and a vomit he turned over onto his back, a corpse.
While the two headsmen were busy tying cords to his flukes and otherwise getting the great mass ready to tow, the two of them fell into conversation.
"I wonder what the old man wants with this lump of foul lard," said Stubb, somewhat disgusted at the thought of dealing with such a lowly leviathan.

"Wants with it?" said Flask, coiling some spare line in the boat's bow. "Did you never hear that the ship which even once has a Sperm Whale's head hoisted on her starboard side, and at the same time a Right Whale's on the port side — did you never hear, Stubb, that that ship can never afterward capsize?"
"Why not?"

"I don't know, but I heard that yellowish ghost of a Fedallah saying so, and he seems to know all about ships' charms. But I sometimes think he'll charm the ship to no good in the end. I don't half like that fellow, Stubb. Did you ever notice how that tusk of his is sort of carved into a snake's head, Stubb?"

"Sink him! I never look at him at all. But if I ever get the chance on a dark night, with him standing close by the bulwarks and nobody around — look down there, Flask" — pointing into the sea with a peculiar motion of both hands — "yes, I will! Flask, I take that Fedallah for the devil in disguise. Do you believe that cock-and-bull story about him being stowed away on board? He's the devil, I tell you. The reason you don't see his tail is that he tucks it up out of sight; he carries it coiled up in his pocket, I guess. Blast him! Now that I think of it, he's always asking for oakum to stuff into the toes of his boots."
"He sleeps in his boots, doesn't he? He hasn't got any hammock, but I've seen him lie at night in a coil of rigging."
"No doubt — and it's because of his cursed tail. He coils it down, do you see, in the eye of the rigging."
"What's the old man have so much to do with him for?"
"Striking up a swap or a bargain, I suppose."
"Bargain? — about what?"

"Why, do you see, the old man is dead set on that White Whale, and the devil there is trying to come around him and get him to swap away his silver watch, or his soul, or something of that sort, and then he'll deliver Moby Dick."
"Nonsense! Stubb, you are joking. How can Fedallah do that?"

"I don't know, Flask, but the devil is a curious fellow, and a wicked one, I tell you. Why, they say he went sauntering into the old flagship once, switching his tail about, devilish easy and gentlemanlike, and asking if the old governor was at home. Well, he was at home, and asked the devil what he wanted. The devil, switching his hoofs, up and says, 'I want John.' 'What for?' says the old governor. 'What business is that of yours?' says the devil, getting mad — 'I want to use him.' 'Take him,' says the governor — and by the Lord, Flask, if the devil didn't give John the Asiatic cholera before he was through with him, I'll eat this whale in one mouthful. But look sharp — aren't you all ready there? Well, then, pull ahead, and let's get the whale alongside."
"I think I remember some story like the one you were telling," said Flask, when at last the two boats were slowly advancing with their burden toward the ship. "But I can't remember where I heard it."
"Three Spaniards? Adventures of those three bloody-minded soldiers? Did you read it there, Flask? I guess you did?"
"No — never saw such a book. Heard of it, though. But now, tell me, Stubb — do you suppose that devil you were speaking of just now was the same you say is now on board the Pequod?"

"Am I the same man who helped kill this whale? Doesn't the devil live forever? Whoever heard of the devil dying? Did you ever see a parson in mourning for the devil? And if the devil has a latchkey to let himself into the admiral's cabin, don't you think he can crawl through a porthole? Tell me that, Mr. Flask?"
"How old do you suppose Fedallah is, Stubb?"

"Do you see that mainmast there?" pointing to the ship. "Well, that's the figure one. Now take all the hoops in the Pequod's hold, and string them along in a row with that mast, for zeros, do you see? Well, that wouldn't even begin to be Fedallah's age. Not all the coopers in creation could show hoops enough to make zeros enough."

"But see here, Stubb, I thought you boasted a little just now that you meant to give Fedallah a toss in the sea if you got a good chance. Now, if he's as old as all those hoops of yours come to, and if he's going to live forever, what good will it do to pitch him overboard — tell me that?"
"Give him a good ducking, anyway."
"But he'd crawl back."
"Duck him again, and keep ducking him."
"Suppose he should take it into his head to duck you, though — yes, and drown you — what then?"

"I'd like to see him try it. I'd give him such a pair of black eyes he wouldn't dare show his face in the admiral's cabin again for a good long while, let alone down in the orlop there, where he lives, or around here on the upper decks, where he sneaks about so much. Damn the devil, Flask — so you think I'm afraid of the devil? Who's afraid of him, except the old governor, who doesn't dare catch him and clap him in double-darbies — double handcuffs — as he deserves, but lets him go around kidnapping people? Yes, and he even signed a bond with him that he'd roast for him all the people the devil kidnapped. There's a governor for you!"
"Do you suppose Fedallah wants to kidnap Captain Ahab?"

"Do I think so? You'll find out before long, Flask. But from now on I'm going to keep a sharp lookout on him, and if I see anything very suspicious going on, I'll just grab him by the scruff of the neck and say — Look here, Beelzebub, don't you do it. And if he makes any fuss, by the Lord, I'll reach into his pocket for his tail, take it to the capstan, and give it such a wrench and heave that it snaps clean off at the stump — do you see? And then, I rather guess, when he finds himself docked in that odd way, he'll slink off without even the poor satisfaction of feeling his tail between his legs."
"And what will you do with the tail, Stubb?"
"Do with it? Sell it for an ox whip when we get home — what else?"
"Now, do you mean what you say, and have been saying all along, Stubb?"
"Mean or not mean, here we are at the ship."
The boats were now hailed to tow the whale on the port side, where fluke chains and other gear were already prepared for securing him.
"Didn't I tell you so?" said Flask. "Yes, you'll soon see this right whale's head hoisted up opposite that sperm whale's."

In good time, Flask's saying proved true. As before, the Pequod had leaned steeply over toward the sperm whale's head; now, by the counterweight of both heads, she regained her even keel — though sorely strained, you may well believe. So, when on one side you hoist in Locke's head, you go over that way; but now, on the other side, hoist in Kant's and you come back again — but in very poor shape. Thus some minds forever keep trimming boat. Oh, you foolish ones! Throw all these thunder-heads overboard, and then you will float light and right.

When the body of a right whale is brought alongside the ship to be dealt with, the same preliminary steps usually take place as with a sperm whale; the difference is that the sperm whale's head is cut off whole, whereas the right whale's lips and tongue are removed separately and hoisted on deck, together with all the familiar black bone (the baleen, or whalebone) attached to what is called the crown-piece. But in this case nothing of the kind had been done. Both carcasses had drifted astern, and the ship, weighed down with heads, looked rather like a mule carrying a pair of overloaded panniers.

Meanwhile, Fedallah was calmly eyeing the right whale's head, and every now and then glancing from the deep wrinkles there to the lines in his own hand. And Ahab happened to stand so that the Parsee occupied his shadow; while, if the Parsee's shadow was there at all, it seemed only to blend with and lengthen Ahab's. As the crew toiled on, Laplandish speculations were bandied about among them concerning all these passing things.
